newsitem.title: UK: Britain urges more Belarus political progress.
newsitem.headline: Britain urges more Belarus political progress.

text.p: Britain's Foreign Office welcomed a political compromise sealed in Belarus on Friday but said more must be done to defuse tensions in the former Soviet republic.

"The compromise which seems to have been agreed is obviously a first step in defusing the tension but there's a way still to go and it's important for both sides to keep talking to each other and for issues to be freely debated in the media," said a Foreign Office spokesman.
Earlier in Minsk, opponents signed a deal to resolve the standoff between President Alexander Lukashenko and parliament.
Lukashenko agreed that results of a controversial referendum set for Sunday on extending his presidential powers would not be binding. In return, parliament would not try to impeach him.
But Western Europe -- alarmed at the Belarussian president's plans to garner fresh powers -- may be harder to please.
Many in the West have made clear they regard Lukashenko as a maverick and have effectively backed the parliament, where critics accuse him of dictatorial tendencies.
Friday's deal had done little to change that.
The Foreign Office said it was still calling in the Belarussian ambassador for high-level talks on Friday, in line with plans it set before the constitutional compromise.
"We will still be expressing our concern," said the spokesman.

He said events over the weekend could affect European Union talks in Brussels on Monday, when members who have not signed on to the idea of closer trade ties with Minsk "will probably pause before doing so to wait and see how things go".
